notes: How this part was researched: the session's shared web-search allowance was already used up (200 of 200) before this part's first search, so nothing here comes from a search. Everything was read directly, one page at a time, with the kit's honest User-Agent (states/net.py) and each site's robots.txt obeyed (for the kit's name and for Claude's named agents): the campaign websites the candidates filed with the Secretary of State (read from sl_websites in the real database, opened read-only), each county's, city's and school district's own pages, the Minnesota DFL's list of endorsed candidates and the House District 66B Republicans' site. A campaign site nobody filed could not be looked for, so a missing website here is not proof that none exists.

Not read, and nothing worked around: Andrew Tweeten's filed site (www.judgetweeten.com has no address on the network today, by the kit's reader and by the reading tool) and the Minnesota Judicial Branch's site (other parts found it refuses scripts; not asked), so the judge has no findings; Nobles County's site (an empty page without scripts), so Gene Metz has no findings; Three Rivers Park District's site (its robots.txt asks scripts to stay out); Marshall Public Schools' site (its pages are drawn by script), so nothing for Bob Prince; Dodge County's Attorney page names no one, so nothing for Crysta Parkin.

Looked for on the government's own page and not there as a sitting member, so nothing is recorded: A. Bradley "Brad" DeBoer (Sibley County's board page lists another commissioner for District 5), Tony Jurowski (Owatonna's Mayor & City Council page), Michael Sorvig (Champlin's Mayor & City Council page lists another member for Ward 2), Tracy N. Frederick (Mankato Area Public Schools' board page), Earl Smith (Elk River's School Board Members page), Kent Holme (Monticello's School Board page names him only in its list of six 2026 candidates).

For the second reader: (1) Todd County writes "Kim Bosl" where our list has Kimberly Bosl; the tie is the county and the office sought. (2) No start years are given where the government's page states only the current term (Ripka, Graupmann, Hilgart, T'Kach, Morris, Fagerlie, Petersen, Bosl, Anderson). ISD 622's board page also carries a 2018 results table with Caleb Anderson's name first, but the page does not say in words that he was elected then. Steve Morris's own site says he is finishing his second term on the City Council, without years. (3) Sarah Larsen's 'from' is the first year in the district's own "Member (2022-2026)"; that may be the election year rather than the year the term began. (4) Kathleen Bart's endorsement is on the home page of the House District 66B Republicans, a unit inside Senate District 66; the sentence is a post on that page and may move down or off it. (5) Aaron Petersen: the filed address with www fails its certificate check (the certificate is for another name); certificate checking was not turned off, and the address without www answers. Only the page's title could be read. (6) Mary T'Kach's Planning Commission service comes from her own site, with no years; her other listed bodies (a task force, a team, a committee) were left out as not clearly public offices. (7) Kathleen Bart's and Darci Smith's sites speak about parties in passing, but neither carries an explicit party or endorsement statement short enough to quote, so no own_words; Declan McCrory's Endorsements page shows no party.

Read and left out on purpose: family, upbringing, schools, jobs and employers, union posts, committee mailing addresses printed on campaign and county pages, and seats on advisory or association boards.

Verifier, 2026-10-02: every address in this file was opened again with the kit's reader and each recorded fact was found on its page. Three wordings were corrected: the clauses citing a second page ("calls him/her an incumbent") were dropped from Sarah Larsen's and Caleb Anderson's sources, because that page is not the one cited, and Anderson's source now carries the term end the page states; Mary T'Kach's Planning Commission entry no longer names the city, since her sentence does not. Nothing was removed.
